title: The Secret to .NET Performance: Generational GC

scenes.say: Ever wonder how .NET apps manage memory so quickly, even under heavy load? Let's break down the secret sauce.

scenes.label: CLR
scenes.sub: The Common Language Runtime runs your .NET code.
scenes.say: First, the Common Language Runtime, or CLR, is the engine that runs your .NET code and manages memory for you.
The real trick is generational garbage collection. Objects start in generation zero. If they survive, they move up to generation one, and eventually to generation two.

scenes.label: LOH
scenes.sub: Large Object Heap holds big objects over 85 kilobytes.
scenes.say: Big objects, over eighty-five kilobytes, go straight to the Large Object Heap. This heap is collected less often, which can lead to memory fragmentation.
Most collections happen in generation zero. It's fast and frequent. Generation two and the Large Object Heap are cleaned up less often, to avoid slowing your app.

scenes.question: Where do memory leaks often hide?
scenes.right: In Gen 2 or the Large Object Heap, since they're collected rarely.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: memory leaks usually hide in generation two or the Large Object Heap, not in generation zero.
